clue.text: During fit of resentment, remove old gemstone

indicators.note: during puts the following pieces within the fit of resentment

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking or peevishness
to rid is to remove

explanation.surface: In a huff, someone throws out an old jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' suggests a seizure, but a pet is a sulk.
explanation.definitionFit: Peridot is a green gem variety of the mineral olivine.

clue.text: Amazing hit, say, for Bush

indicators.note: amazing is read as putting into a maze, scrambling the three words

explanation.surface: A stunning success, for example, for George Bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' wants to be the US president, but it is a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsythia is a shrub with yellow spring flowers, so a bush.

clue.text: For instance, Wolves, in an irregular formation?

definitions.text: For instance, Wolves, in an irregular formation?

parts.words: For instance, Wolves, in an irregular formation?
parts.note: the football club suggests a team shape, but the word wolves is formed irregularly from wolf, so it is a grammatical example

explanation.definitionFit: Wolves is the plural of wolf, formed irregularly by changing f to v.

clue.text: Test with erroneous number

indicators.note: erroneous says the letters of the two words before it are set down wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: An exam paper carries a wrong figure somewhere in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like the mistaken figure, but it is the definition: a number is a song or dance routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a song or dance routine, and this 1960s dance craze and its record are one.

clue.text: Model got Bowie nothing until later

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so these words are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A model got nothing from David Bowie until much later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a person, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means for the time being, until something more is done later.

clue.text: Difficult old flame is over histrionics

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, an old flame
histrionics is theatrical acting

explanation.surface: A former lover is done with dramatic tantrums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is over' suggests finished with, but in a down light it means placed above.
explanation.definitionFit: Exacting means demanding, so difficult to satisfy.

clue.text: Cheeky boy's introduction to White Album by The Beatles

indicators.note: introduction to picks out the first letter of the next word

parts.note: Help! is a 1965 album by the Beatles

explanation.surface: A lad's first taste of the Beatles' White Album.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White Album' looks like one Beatles record, but 'White' gives only W and the album is another.
explanation.definitionFit: A whelp is a young pup, and figuratively an impudent youth.

clue.text: Space in water to turn, manoeuvring some oar

indicators.note: manoeuvring means moving around, so these letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A rower needs room on the river to turn the boat with an oar.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea room is the open water a ship needs to manoeuvre without hazard.

clue.text: Cow bird of prey's heard in soil

indicators.note: heard means the words that come before are spoken, and the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: beef is the meat of the cow, so cow can stand for beef; an owl is a bird of prey that hunts at night

explanation.surface: A heifer and a hawk, oddly, are listened to in the dirt of a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' reads as a verb meaning intimidate, but here it gives BEEF; said together with OWL it makes a word meaning to dirty.
explanation.definitionFit: To soil something is to dirty or make it foul, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Part of car that's initially becoming flat perhaps following scrape

indicators.note: following says the flat comes after the scrape in the answer
initially picks out the opening letter of the word after it

parts.note: to rake is to scrape, as with a rake across ground
a pad is slang for a flat or home, so a flat is one example

explanation.surface: Something on a car goes flat after being scraped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' suggests a punctured tyre, but it is a home: PAD, as in bachelor pad.
explanation.definitionFit: This friction block presses on the disc to slow a vehicle, so it is one component of a car.

clue.text: Depart with teacher, each going over Latin hymn

parts.note: to die is to depart this life
sir is how British pupils address a male teacher

indicators.note: going over says the abbreviation for each is turned around

explanation.surface: Leaving with a schoolmaster, everyone runs through a Latin hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' reads as rehearsing, but it turns EA into AE.
explanation.definitionFit: This medieval sequence on the Day of Judgement is sung in the Latin Requiem Mass, so it is a Latin hymn.

clue.text: Class returning drug after warning

indicators.note: after puts the drug following the warning in the answer

parts.note: a tip, or tip-off, is a warning given in advance

indicators.note: returning says the drug word comes back, read from its end

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A school class goes back to drugs after being warned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class' looks like a noun, a group of pupils, but it is an adjective meaning first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Class used as an adjective means excellent, just as tip-top means of the highest quality.

clue.text: One of two jokers from Liverpool let socialist back

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A comedian from a Liverpool double act lets a left-winger return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' signals that the letters are taken out of the three words that follow; read backwards, LOOL LET SOC gives the comic's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lou Costello was one half of the comedy double act Abbott and Costello.

clue.text: Bungle I mention before you know it

indicators.note: to bungle is to mess something up, so these letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: I fluff my speech, and it happens before I realise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bungle' looks like the verb of the surface, but it is the signal to rearrange I MENTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean very quickly, almost instantly, an idiomatic equivalence.

clue.text: I'll get a bit of food out, and also most of the cream

definitions.text: I'll get a bit of food out

parts.note: too means as well, and also

indicators.note: most of drops the last letter of the short word that follows

parts.note: the pick of something is its cream, the best

explanation.surface: Someone will remove a morsel and also skim most of the cream.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the object: it says it will dislodge food from teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A dental stick says this because its job is to remove scraps of food from between teeth.

clue.text: Ship's fixture extra secure when male and female swap places

indicators.text: when male and female swap places
indicators.note: the abbreviations for male and female trade places between the two words

parts.note: more means extra
fast means firmly fixed, secure

explanation.surface: Something on a ship is made doubly secure when men and women change places.
explanation.walkthrough: M and F, the abbreviations for male and female, swap between MORE and FAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A foremast is the mast nearest the bow, a fixed part of a ship.

clue.text: Hit it off and make out

definitions.meaning: to hit it off is to be friendly with someone
to make out is to manage or cope

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to be on friendly terms and to manage adequately, two idiomatic senses.

clue.text: Maybe Dubai house with no roof upset English sailor

indicators.note: with no roof takes the top letter off the house word, since in a down light the first letter is the roof

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house

indicators.note: upset turns the two pieces upside down, which in a down light reads them backwards

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A Dubai home with its top missing annoys an English sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses E and TAR together, giving RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is one of the seven states of the United Arab Emirates, so it is an example.

clue.text: Called up Light, rough and weather-beaten!

indicators.note: in a down light, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: rang means called on the phone
an LED is a light-emitting diode, a light

explanation.surface: The setter Light is called on and found to be rough and worn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' is the setter's own name, which makes the surface self-mocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnarled means knotty, twisted and roughened, as by age or weather.

clue.text: Suggestion of surplus weight with little energy

parts.note: over means in excess, surplus
a ton is a unit of weight
E is the abbreviation for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A hint that someone is carrying extra pounds and has little get-up-and-go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little energy' is a single letter, not a lack of vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: An overtone is an implied hint or nuance, so a suggestion.

clue.text: Recalls reasonable Ballesteros tipping over bags

indicators.note: bags means takes in, so the golfer's name holds the other piece
tipping over turns the golfer's name upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: Seve Ballesteros was a Spanish golfer
OK means reasonable, acceptable

explanation.surface: Fair-minded Seve Ballesteros knocks over golf bags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bags' reads as golf bags, but it is a verb, holding OK.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to call to mind, so to recall.

clue.text: One grand left to plug function

indicators.note: to plug says the two letters go into the function word, filling a gap in it

parts.note: the sine is a trigonometric function
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A thousand pounds is left over to fund a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One grand' reads as a sum of money, but 'One' is the definition and only 'grand' gives a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Single means one only, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Understand lawn must be cut quietly

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the lawn word loses its last letter

parts.note: grass covers a lawn
P is piano, quietly in music

explanation.surface: Grasp that the lawn needs mowing quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' suggests mowing, but it takes S off GRASS.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp an idea is to understand it.

clue.text: Lies with son, taking in cricket maybe

indicators.note: taking in says the two outer letters surround the insect word

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies
a hopper is a leaping insect, and a cricket is one example

explanation.surface: Someone tells fibs with their son, perhaps over a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cricket' suggests the sport, but it is the insect: a hopper.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoppers are big, blatant lies, a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: A ham actor oddly beginning to imitate dancing participant in espionage

indicators.note: dancing says the gathered letters move about into a new order
oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of the word after it
beginning to picks the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An overacting performer starts mimicking a dancer who was really a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram pool is A, HAM, ATR (actor's odd letters) and I. The surface hints at the answer, an exotic dancer who was shot as a spy in 1917.
explanation.definitionFit: Mata Hari, the Dutch dancer, was executed as a German spy, so she took part in espionage.

clue.text: Impresses blighters when downing whiskey, right?

indicators.note: downing means putting down or dropping, so these letters leave the word

parts.note: wretches and blighters are both contemptible people
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Rotters make an impression by knocking back whisky, don't they?
explanation.walkthrough: 'downing' looks like drinking, but it means dropping W and R from WRETCHES.
explanation.definitionFit: To impress is to press a mark into a surface, and to etch is to engrave one.

clue.text: In front of chief, journalist reviewed brief flood report

indicators.note: in front of places the earlier pieces before the chief
reviewed is read as re-viewed, looked at the other way round

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a senior journalist

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the flood word loses its last letter

parts.note: a spate is a flood, as of a river

explanation.surface: A journalist goes over a short flood report before the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flood report' looks like the subject, but 'report' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A despatch is an official report, as from a war correspondent.
